newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-FROST SHOOTS COURSE RECORD 63.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FROST SHOOTS COURSE RECORD 63.

text.p: South African David Frost shot a course record nine-under-par 63 to move to within one shot of the lead at the halfway stage of the South African PGA championship on Friday.
He trailed fellow countryman Retief Goosen who added a 66 to his first round 65.
Frost, starting at the 10th hole, was out in 35, one under. He then stormed home in a remarkable 28 shots, finishing birdie, eagle, birdie, eagle.
Frost, who shared second place with Germany's Thomas Gogele, whose course record he broke, said he had missed some makeable putts going out but "made up for it coming home.
"The best was on the eighth (Frost's 17th, a par three) where I hit an awful nine iron to the extreme left of the green and holed a 50-footer for birdie."
Zimbabwe's Nick Price, a winner in Sun City last week, and Italy's Massimo Scarpa were a shot further back at 11 under. Price carded a 66 and Scarpa 68.
It was another disappointing day for European Ryder Cup captain Severiano Ballesteros. His 73 meant he missed the cut by seven shots.
